stem: In the equation \(\frac{x + k}{3} - \frac{x - 2}{4} = \frac{x}{12} + 2\), \(k\) is a constant. If the equation has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of \(k\)?
solution: Multiply every term by 12: \(4(x + k) - 3(x - 2) = x + 24\).
The \(x\)-terms already match, so the equation is true for all \(x\) exactly when \(4k + 6 = 24\).
So \(k = \frac{18}{4} = \frac{9}{2}\), or 4.5. (For any other \(k\) there is no solution.)
verify:
x, k = symbols('x k')
d = expand(12*((x + k)/3 - (x - 2)/4 - x/12 - 2))
assert d.coeff(x, 1) == 0
kv = solve(d, k)
assert kv == [Rational(9, 2)]
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == kv
